newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - May 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - May 15.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Thursday:
* The dollar dropped to a four-month low of 117.20 Japanese yen and fell against other currencies as well.
* Dutch financial services group Internationale Nederlanden Groep NV dropped out of talks to purchase U.S. investment bank Dillon Read.
* Riser Foods Inc has reached an agreement to merge with privately held Giant Eagle Inc, a retail supermarket chain and wholesale distributor.
* Bondholders fighting Marvel Entertainment Group Inc's plan to merge with Toy Biz Inc won the right in court to vote their 80 percent stake.
* Philip Morris Cos Inc said the Federal Trade Commission was investigating how it distributes its cigarettes.
* Standard & Poor's Corp raised the credit ratings of Hong Kong and China.
* Officials and traders said that China has replaced its top securities regulator, a possible sign it plans to clamp down on the country's volatile market.
* Three former executives of Nomura Securities Co Ltd have been arrested on charges of illegally paying money to racketeers.
* Environmentally-minded rebels of Shell Transport & Trading Co Plc, the British arm of the Royal Dutch/Shell Group failed in their bid for tougher "green" policies.
* Star Alliance, an alliance of a group of airline companies, outlined their partnership.
* A federal regulatory agency has withheld approval of the merger of Wisconsin Energy Corp and Northern States Power Co.
* The U.S. Post Office has been battered by non-government rivals, forcing federal policymakers to take their first hard look at the agency in 25 years.
* Prices paid to American manufacturers and other producers fell 0.6 percent in April, the largest monthly drop in close to four years.

* Response USA Inc last summer issued an unusual preferred security that led to a drop in its stock price. On Wednesday, it reached a deal with Halifax Fund LP to convert its preferred security and sell the underlying common stock to certain unaffiliated purchasers.
